cards.name: IAction
cards.path: PhotoshopTypeLibrary/IAction
cards.summary: Legacy OLE Actions COM interface for one recorded action from the Actions panel: read its name and play it on the active document. Part of the old Photoshop Type Library, separate from the scripting DOM.
use_for: replay a recorded house action (web resize + sharpen, watermark) on the open document from a COM client
list the loaded actions by name before choosing which one to run
avoid: new automation: the scripting DOM's app.doAction(action, from) names both the action and its set
running with no document open: Play always targets the active document
cards.how: Reached from the legacy IActions collection: IPhotoshopApplication.Actions.Item(i) returns an IAction. name gives the action's name, Play runs it on the active document. Legacy Photoshop Type Library (TypeLibrary.tlb, the OLE Actions automation layer); the harvest does not show which ProgID binds to it in 27.4 (unverified).

key_members.name: name
key_members.use: read-only name of the action as shown in the Actions panel

key_members.name: Play
key_members.use: plays the action on the active document; no arguments, returns nothing

gotchas: Play takes no target: make the right document active first (IAutoPSDoc.Activate)
only the action name is exposed, not its set, so two sets holding an action of the same name cannot be told apart (unverified)
an action step that needs a selection or a pixel layer fails inside Play as a COM error or a blocking dialog (unverified)
binding to this legacy object model from Python / VBScript in 27.4 is not confirmed by the harvest (unverified)
cards.example:
# app: legacy IPhotoshopApplication (TypeLibrary.tlb)
acts = app.Actions
for i in range(acts.count):          # index base unverified
    a = acts.Item(i)
    if a.name == 'Web Resize':
        a.Play()

cards.name: IActionControl
cards.path: PhotoshopTypeLibrary/IActionControl
cards.summary: Legacy OLE Actions control object: plays any Action Manager event by numeric ID with a parameter descriptor, reads properties through a reference, and converts between string IDs and numeric type IDs. The COM ancestor of the DOM's executeAction / executeActionGet / stringIDToTypeID.
use_for: play a filter or command that has no DOM method (an event captured with ScriptListener) from a COM client
read a document or layer property the DOM does not expose, via GetActionProperty
translate stringIDs such as 'gaussianBlur' into the numeric IDs that descriptor keys need
avoid: new automation: the DOM Application's executeAction / executeActionGet / stringIDToTypeID do the same job and return values instead of filling byref out-parameters
cards.how: Created with IPhotoshopApplication.MakeControlObject(). Play(eventID, parameters, dialogOptions) runs an event: eventID is a numeric type ID (a PSConstants phEvent* value or StringIDToTypeID result), parameters an IActionDescriptor, dialogOptions a PSConstants dialog value: phDialogDontDisplay 0, phDialogDisplay 1, phDialogSilent 2. Play returns the result descriptor. Legacy Photoshop Type Library (TypeLibrary.tlb, the OLE Actions automation layer); the harvest does not show which ProgID binds to it in 27.4 (unverified).

key_members.name: Play
key_members.use: run an event (eventID, parameter descriptor, dialog mode); returns the result IActionDescriptor

key_members.name: GetActionProperty
key_members.use: read the property a reference points at into a descriptor (byref propertyDesc)

key_members.name: StringIDToTypeID
key_members.use: stringID ('gaussianBlur', 'radius') to numeric type ID, delivered through the byref typeID

key_members.name: TypeIDToStringID
key_members.use: numeric type ID back to its stringID, delivered through the byref stringID

gotchas: StringIDToTypeID, TypeIDToStringID and GetActionProperty return void and hand the result back through a byref parameter (harvested signatures); late-bound callers must handle out-parameters (win32com usually returns them as the call result, unverified)
dialogOptions is a plain long: pass 0 (phDialogDontDisplay) or 2 (phDialogSilent) in unattended runs, 1 opens the event's dialog and blocks the call
Play needs a descriptor even for events without settings: pass an empty one from MakeDescriptor (unverified whether a null is accepted)
type IDs for stringID-only terms are assigned at run time; resolve them each session instead of hard-coding the numbers (unverified)
cards.example:
ctl = app.MakeControlObject()        # app: legacy IPhotoshopApplication
desc = app.MakeDescriptor()
phEventGaussianBlur, phKeyRadius = 1198747202, 1382314784
phUnitPixels = 592476268              # PSConstants values from the harvest
desc.PutUnitDouble(phKeyRadius, phUnitPixels, 8.0)
ctl.Play(phEventGaussianBlur, desc, 0)   # 0 = phDialogDontDisplay

cards.name: IActionDescriptor
cards.path: PhotoshopTypeLibrary/IActionDescriptor
cards.summary: Legacy OLE Actions key/value container: holds the parameters of an Action Manager event or the properties returned by one. Every value is keyed by a numeric type ID and written with a typed Put* or read with a typed Get* method.
use_for: build the settings of a filter or command (radius, amount, mode) before IActionControl.Play
read back a returned descriptor (layer bounds, document size) after GetActionProperty
nest objects such as a colour or an offset with PutObject for Fill / Make events
avoid: new automation: the DOM ActionDescriptor class (createable over COM) returns values directly instead of through byref out-parameters
cards.how: Created with IPhotoshopApplication.MakeDescriptor(); passed to IActionControl.Play or filled by IActionControl.GetActionProperty. Keys, class IDs, enum types and unit IDs are all longs (PSConstants ph* values or StringIDToTypeID results). The harvest pairs it with the DOM ActionDescriptor (compare_omv): every Get*/Put* here is TypeLibrary-only. Legacy Photoshop Type Library (TypeLibrary.tlb, the OLE Actions automation layer); the harvest does not show which ProgID binds to it in 27.4 (unverified).

booleans are longs here (PutBoolean, GetBoolean, HasKey, IsEqual), not COM booleans
a plain PutDouble where the event expects a unit double is rejected or misread (unverified)
GetData / PutData move raw bytes as a string; binary data can be mangled by string conversion over COM (unverified)

ctl = app.MakeControlObject()        # app: legacy IPhotoshopApplication
d = app.MakeDescriptor()
phKeyAmount, phUnitPercent = 1097690740, 592474723
d.PutUnitDouble(phKeyAmount, phUnitPercent, 50.0)
print(d.GetCount())                  # out-param returned (unverified)
print(d.HasKey(phKeyAmount))

cards.name: IActionReference
cards.path: PhotoshopTypeLibrary/IActionReference
cards.summary: Legacy OLE Actions reference that points an event at its target: a class plus a form (name, index, identifier, offset, enumerated or property), chained through containers, e.g. 'the layer named Logo in the current document'.
use_for: target a specific layer, channel or document for an event without selecting it
name the single property to read when calling IActionControl.GetActionProperty
address the current target with an enumerated form (ordinal / target)
avoid: new automation: the DOM ActionReference with app.executeActionGet returns the descriptor directly
cards.how: Created with IPhotoshopApplication.MakeReference(). Each Put* adds one level (desired class plus form value); GetForm tells the form of the current level and GetContainer walks to the next one. Passed inside a descriptor (IActionDescriptor.PutReference under the null key) or straight to GetActionProperty. Legacy Photoshop Type Library (TypeLibrary.tlb, the OLE Actions automation layer); the harvest does not show which ProgID binds to it in 27.4 (unverified).

all Get* return through byref parameters; GetEnumerated yields both the enum type and the value

cards.name: IAutoPSDoc

cards.summary: Legacy OLE automation handle on an open image document: its title, making it the active target, saving a copy under another name, and closing it (which saves).
use_for: open a file, activate it and run a recorded action on it from a COM client
write a processed copy next to the original while keeping it open
avoid: discarding changes: Close saves, use the DOM Document.close with SaveOptions.DONOTSAVECHANGES
anything about layers, size or pixels: go through IActionControl events or the DOM Document

key_members.name: SaveTo

cards.name: ActionDescriptor
cards.path: Actions/ActionDescriptor
cards.summary: Scripting-DOM Action Manager record of key/value pairs: the parameters handed to app.executeAction and the properties returned by app.executeActionGet. The route to any Photoshop command or property the DOM does not wrap.
use_for: apply a filter, adjustment or layer command with exact settings (ScriptListener-style code)
read layer, document or app properties the DOM lacks (smart object info, layer IDs, bounds without effects)
batch tasks that must run with no dialogs (DialogModes.NO)
avoid: simple tasks the DOM already wraps (resizeImage, saveAs, artLayers.add): DOM calls are easier to read
hard-coding descriptors copied from one Photoshop version without testing them on 27.4
cards.how: ExtendScript: new ActionDescriptor(), filled with typed put calls and passed to app.executeAction(eventID, descriptor, DialogModes.NO). COM: the createable coclass ActionDescriptor (interface _ActionDescriptor, harvested under extra.com) with PutString, PutInteger, PutUnitDouble, PutEnumerated, PutReference, PutObject, PutList, PutBoolean, PutClass, PutPath, PutLargeInteger and the matching getters (GetUnitDoubleValue, GetEnumerationValue, GetObjectValue ...), plus HasKey, GetKey, GetType, Count, Clear, Erase. Keys are numeric IDs from app.stringIDToTypeID / app.charIDToTypeID.

key_members.name: count
key_members.use: number of keys in the descriptor (the only member the ExtendScript reflection recorded; the typed get/put methods are on the COM interface)

gotchas: harvest gap: the ExtendScript side reflected only count; the get/put method list comes from the COM interface, and the ExtendScript spellings are the same names in lowerCamel case (unverified against this harvest)
COM getters here return values directly (GetUnitDoubleValue plus GetUnitDoubleType), unlike the legacy IActionDescriptor which fills byref parameters
unit doubles need the right unit ID (pixelsUnit, percentUnit, angleUnit); a wrong unit is converted or rejected (unverified)
GetType returns a DescValueType (INTEGERTYPE, UNITDOUBLE, OBJECTTYPE ...); check it before reading a key of unknown type
type IDs of stringID-only terms are assigned at run time; never hard-code them across sessions (unverified)
the COM ProgID Photoshop.ActionDescriptor is the usual way to create it from Python (unverified in this harvest)
cards.example:
import win32com.client
app = win32com.client.Dispatch('Photoshop.Application')
d = win32com.client.Dispatch('Photoshop.ActionDescriptor')
s = app.StringIDToTypeID
d.PutUnitDouble(s('radius'), s('pixelsUnit'), 8.0)
# needs an open document with a pixel layer active
app.ExecuteAction(s('gaussianBlur'), d, 3)   # 3 = psDisplayNoDialogs
print(d.Count)

cards.summary: Scripting-DOM Action Manager list: an ordered, append-only list of values (references, numbers, strings, nested descriptors) for event parameters that take several items, such as selecting several layers or giving curve points.
use_for: select or link several layers in one executeAction call
pass curve points, gradient stops or channel lists to an adjustment
read list properties (target layers, fonts) out of an executeActionGet result
avoid: a single value: put it straight into the ActionDescriptor
cards.how: ExtendScript: new ActionList(), filled with typed put calls and stored in a descriptor with putList. COM: the createable coclass ActionList (interface _ActionList, extra.com) with Put* (append, no index), Get*(Index), GetType(Index), Count and Clear.

key_members.name: count
key_members.use: number of items (the only member the ExtendScript reflection recorded; the typed methods are on the COM interface)

gotchas: Put* methods append; there is no insert or replace, so rebuild the list to change it
the harvested class description ('the list of commands that comprise an Action') is misleading: it is a generic value list
harvest gap: only count was reflected on the ExtendScript side; method names come from the COM interface (lowerCamel in ExtendScript, unverified against this harvest)
lists are normally one value type per event parameter; mixing types may be rejected (unverified)
cards.example:
import win32com.client
app = win32com.client.Dispatch('Photoshop.Application')
lst = win32com.client.Dispatch('Photoshop.ActionList')
ref = win32com.client.Dispatch('Photoshop.ActionReference')
ref.PutName(app.StringIDToTypeID('layer'), 'Logo')
lst.PutReference(ref)
print(lst.Count)

cards.name: ActionReference

use_for: read one property of the active layer or document with executeActionGet
target a layer by ID for an executeAction without selecting it first
address 'current' items with ordinal / targetEnum
avoid: walking many layers by index in a large file: put a property level first so executeActionGet returns only that property (unverified speed-up)

cards.example:
import win32com.client
app = win32com.client.Dispatch('Photoshop.Application')
s = app.StringIDToTypeID

ref.PutProperty(s('property'), s('bounds'))
ref.PutEnumerated(s('layer'), s('ordinal'), s('targetEnum'))
desc = app.ExecuteActionGet(ref)
